rows.question: My house faces a 10 m wide street and will be 9 m tall. How much open space do I leave at the front?
rows.gold: 3.6 m front open space. Rule 56(1)(a): street more than 9 m and up to 12 m, building up to 12.5 m height (PDF p.77).

answer.answer: The minimum front open space is 3.6 m. Your house is 9 m tall, which is within the 12.5 m limit for this table, and it faces a 10 m street, which falls in the 'more than 9.0 m and up to 12 m' row. The Development Plan of the town can set different norms (Rule 103). Rear and side open spaces depend on plot area and building type, so they are not covered in this answer.
answer.ask_citizen: If the citizen also needs the rear or side open spaces, ask for the plot area, the plot frontage and the building type (detached, semi-detached or row).

rows.question: I want a farm house on agricultural land. What is the minimum plot size and the maximum FAR?
rows.gold: Minimum plot 0.40 hectare, maximum FAR 0.10. Rule 17(a),(b) (PDF p.34).

answer.answer: Under Rule 17, a farm house is allowed in an area designated for agricultural use. The minimum plot size is 0.40 hectare and the maximum FAR is 0.10. Rule 17 also sets these conditions: maximum height of 7.5 meters with a sloping roof, at least 100 live trees per hectare before applying, an access road at least 7.5 meters wide, and at least 7.50 meters of open space (MOS) on all sides. The Authority can add other conditions.

rows.question: My development permission was granted in 2023. How long does it stay valid, and how many times can I renew it?
rows.gold: Valid 3 years; revalidation for two consecutive terms of one year each (5 years max), then apply afresh. If work starts within validity it does not lapse. Rule 23 (PDF p.41).

answer.answer:
- **How long it is valid:** A development permission stays valid for up to 3 years from the date it was granted (Rule 23(1)).
- **How many renewals:** It can be revalidated only twice, for 1 year each time, one after the other. That makes 5 years at most, and this 5-year limit cannot be relaxed. After that, the citizen has to submit the proposal afresh (Rule 23(2)).
- **Renewal fee:** Revalidation is free if the application reaches the Authority before the permission expires. If it is filed after the 3 years have run out, the Authority will charge a permission fee equal to the Rule 21(3)(a) fee before revalidating (Rule 23(2)).
- **If work has started:** If the project began while the permission was still valid, the permission does not lapse at any time afterwards and no revalidation is needed (Rule 23(3)).
answer.ask_citizen: Please ask for the exact date of the 2023 development permission so the 3-year expiry date can be worked out. Also ask whether work on the project has already started.

rows.question: I applied for building permission and the authority has not replied. What happens if they miss the deadline?
rows.gold: Deemed sanctioned if refusal not intimated within the period in Section 30(5) of the Act, but not for applications to an authorised Architect/Structural Engineer, and nothing contrary to Act/Rules/Development Plan is authorised. Rule 28 (PDF p.48-49).

answer.answer: Under Rule 28, if the Authority does not tell the applicant in writing that it has refused sanction within the period set in section 30(5) of the Act, the permission is deemed to be sanctioned. Rule 35(3) calls this the 'period of sixty days under sub-section (5) of section 30'. Deemed sanction has limits. It does not allow anything that goes against the Act and Rules, the Development Plan or Zoning Plan, the lease or title terms, or any other law that applies to the site. It also does not apply to applications filed with an authorised Architect/Structural Engineer: if they miss the deadline, permission is not deemed granted (Rule 28 proviso). Such an architect or engineer must issue permission within 30 days at most (Rule 26-B(1)).
answer.ask_citizen: Ask the citizen: did you file with the Municipal Corporation or with an authorised Architect/Structural Engineer? On what date did you file, and have you received any written refusal or objection?

rows.question: How far must my balcony stay from a low-voltage overhead electric line, vertically and horizontally?
rows.gold: 2.5 m vertically, 1.2 m horizontally (or Electricity Rules if more). Rule 52(1) (PDF p.69).

answer.answer: Under Rule 52, a building has to stay at least 2.5 metres from a low or medium voltage line (or service line) vertically and 1.2 metres horizontally. If the applicable Electricity Rules set a larger distance, the larger one applies. A balcony cannot be built, rebuilt or altered in a way that breaks these limits. The vertical gap is measured from the line's lowest point when it sags the most, and the horizontal gap from its furthest swing in the wind.

rows.question: Who is allowed to sign and submit my building plans?
rows.gold: Licensed architect, structural engineer, engineer, supervisor or town planner, with name, qualification and licence number; owner also signs. Rule 18 (PDF p.34); scope by licence in Rule 26.

answer.answer:
Building plans must be prepared and signed by a qualified professional: an architect, structural engineer, engineer, supervisor or town planner. The professional must show their name, address, qualifications, licence number and its validity. You, as owner or applicant, must also sign the plans and give your address (Rule 18). Who can submit your plans depends on your plot size and building height (Rule 26(9)):
- **Architect** registered with the Council of Architecture: plans for any building, whatever its size or height. No separate licence is needed.
- **Licensed Structural Engineer:** residential buildings on plots up to 500 sq m, and up to three storeys or 11 m high.
- **Licensed Engineer:** residential buildings on plots up to 300 sq m, and up to two storeys or 7.5 m high. A High Court ruling struck down part of this limit and said the Architect's scope applies to Engineers too, so the clerk should check this.
- **Licensed Supervisor:** residential buildings on plots up to 200 sq m, and up to two storeys or 7.5 m high.
answer.ask_citizen: Ask the citizen for the plot area (sq m) and the planned number of storeys or height. These show which licensed professional can submit the plans.

rows.question: What documents go with an application for building permission?
rows.gold: Application in Appendix A-2/A-2(1) with documents, plans and statements (Rule 14); details of information accompanying the application in Rule 16 (ownership documents, site plan, building plan, etc.).

answer.answer:
Under Rule 16(1)(b), a building permission application (form in Appendix A-2) must include:
- the application fee
- a Key Plan and Site Plans
- the Sub-Division/Layout Plan approved under section 30
- Building Plans and Service Plans
- a Project Report on the proposed development
- proof of ownership or another legal right to the site
- the owner's authorisation, if the applicant is not the owner
- parking plans with parking calculations
- a certificate of supervision

For proof of title, Rule 16(11) asks for attested copies of the sale deed or lease deed and of the khasra plan (patwari aks) and khatauni record.

Rule 14(2) also requires a certificate signed by the Structural Engineer, Architect, Engineer or Supervisor confirming that Rule 88 (earthquake provisions) has been followed.

Under Rule 14(1), documents, plans and statements are filed in 4 copies (quadruplicate), with plans in ammonia or white print, plus an electronic copy. If the Authority uses the online system, everything is submitted only through its software.

For a high-rise building, Rule 16(10) also requires a structural stability certificate with calculations.

rows.question: What is the fee for building permission for a residential house?
rows.gold: Application fee Rs 1 per sq m of proposed built-up area (21(2)(ii)) plus permission fee by slab of built-up area, e.g. Rs 750 up to 75 sq m ... Rs 50,000 above 2500 sq m (21(3)(b) item 1, PDF p.36).

answer.answer: I can't give the exact amount yet because the proposed built-up area is missing. For a residential house there are two fees: (1) an application fee of Rs 1.00 per sq m of the proposed built-up area (Rule 21(2)(ii)), and (2) a permission fee from the slab table in Rule 21(3)(b). The permission fee starts at Rs 750 for up to 75 sq m, is Rs 1,250 for 76 to 125 sq m, and goes up to Rs 50,000 for more than 2500 sq m. Once the citizen gives the built-up area, the exact fee can be worked out. Different rates apply to high-rise buildings.
answer.ask_citizen: Please ask the citizen for the total proposed built-up area of the house (sq m, all floors), and whether it is a high-rise building (more than 10 storeys or above 30 m).

rows.question: Can I change my plan after it is sanctioned?
rows.gold: Deviation not permissible if it affects front MOS, exceeds 30% of permissible FAR, parking/public utility, road alignment, water body (Rule 24). Addition/alteration in proposed plan up to 10%: Rs 500; above 10%: fresh application (Rule 21(3)(b) item 8).

answer.answer:
Yes, but only within limits.
- **Small changes:** If the addition or alteration to the sanctioned plan is up to 10%, the fee is Rs. 500.00. If it is above 10%, the citizen must make a fresh application (Rule 21(3)(b), item 8).
- **Changes that are never allowed:** A deviation is not allowed if it affects the front Marginal Open Space or goes beyond 30% of the permissible FAR. It is also not allowed if it concerns the parking area or public utility space, or falls within the road boundary or the alignment of a public road. Changes in a water body (talab), river, nallah or stream, or within 30 meters of the bank of a water body (or the distance set in the development plan), are also not allowed (Rule 24(1)).
- **If the building already differs from the sanctioned plan:** The local authority may charge a compounding fee as prescribed under its own governing Act (Rule 24(3)).
answer.ask_citizen: Ask what change the citizen wants to make, and roughly how big it is compared with the sanctioned plan (up to 10% or more). Also ask whether construction has already started or the change has already been built.

rows.question: Do I need separate development permission for a 300 sq m plot that matches the Development Plan?
rows.gold: Per the 28 Aug 2026 amendment to Rule 2(5)(c) (secondary source): for plots up to 500 sq m conforming to Development Plan land use, the local authority may permit construction; no separate development permission under 2(5)(a). Consolidated text: Rule 2(5)(c) (central area) - must flag version.

answer.answer: The consolidated rules (up to 6 March 2025) do not have a general exemption based on plot size. Here is what they do say: (1) Where land in the Central area of the adopted Development Plan is already developed, the local body issues building permission according to the Development Plan's land use. (2) Building permission comes from the Municipal Corporation. (3) Both development permission and building permission are needed only when building involves developing land as a composite building scheme. If the citizen's 300 sq m plot is a single plot of that kind, only building permission from the Corporation appears to apply. The clerk must confirm the plot's status. A later amendment may exempt the plot outright (see amendment note).
answer.ask_citizen: Ask whether the plot is an individual plot in an approved layout or in an already-developed Central area of the Development Plan, or whether it is part of a composite building scheme or a sub-division.
answer.amendment_note: A later amendment dated 28 August 2026 to Rule 2(5)(c) says the local authority may permit construction or reconstruction on plots of up to 500 sq m that conform to the existing land use in the approved Development Plan, without separate development permission under Rule 2(5)(a), as long as the Development Plan norms are met. If this is in force, it would cover a 300 sq m plot. This comes from a secondary summary (TeamLease RegTech), not the official gazette text, so check it against the official gazette before relying on it.

rows.question: Which rule decides what happens when the Development Plan and these rules disagree?
rows.gold: Rule 103: Development Plan norms apply; if different/contrary, the Director sends a proposal to the Government whose decision is final (PDF p.107).

answer.answer: Rule 103 covers this. In the plan area, the norms set in the relevant Development Plan apply. If the Development Plan's norms differ from or contradict these Rules, the Director must examine the matter and send a proposal to the Government. The Government's decision is final and becomes part of the Development Plan. Rule 61 also says that FAR and density may be adopted as set in the Development Plan of the town.

rows.question: What are the rules for lifts in a building taller than 15 m?
rows.gold: Lifts required for buildings above 12.5 m; per NBC Part VIII Section 5; details in Appendix A-2(A) with application; completion report E-3(A); insurance; maintenance. Rule 83 (PDF p.95).

answer.answer:
Yes, a lift is required. Any building taller than 12.5 m must have one, so a 15 m+ building needs a lift (Rule 83). Under Rule 83, the owner must:
- Plan, design, install, operate, maintain and inspect the lift according to Section 5 of Part-VIII of the National Building Code (NBC).
- Give the lift installation details with the building permission application, in Appendix A-2(A).
- Submit the lift work completion report in Appendix E-3(A) when applying for the completion certificate under Rule 102.
- Insure the lift and the people who use it with a recognised agency.
- Follow the Lift Engineer's maintenance instructions.
- Submit a safety and audit report every 6 months, signed by the Lift Engineer. An individual owner using a lift in their own home does not have to do this.
- Report full details of any accident to the Authority within 24 hours.

rows.question: मेरा प्लॉट 200 वर्ग मीटर का है और सामने 9 मीटर चौड़ी सड़क है। आगे कितनी जगह खाली छोड़नी होगी?
rows.gold: 3.0 मीटर (सड़क 9 मीटर तक). नियम 56(1)(a), PDF p.77.

answer.answer: 9 मीटर चौड़ी सड़क वाले प्लॉट पर आगे कम से कम 3.0 मीटर जगह खाली छोड़नी होगी। यह नियम 56 की तालिका के अनुसार है और 12.5 मीटर तक ऊँचे आवासीय भवन पर लागू होता है। साथ में जानकारी के लिए: 200 वर्ग मीटर के प्लॉट पर पीछे कम से कम 2.5 मीटर जगह खाली छोड़नी होगी।
answer.ask_citizen: नागरिक से पूछें कि भवन की ऊँचाई कितनी होगी। ऊपर बताई गई आगे की खुली जगह 12.5 मीटर तक ऊँचे भवन के लिए है।

rows.question: बिल्डिंग परमिशन की फीस कितनी है और किस नियम में लिखी है?
rows.gold: नियम 21: आवेदन शुल्क ₹1 प्रति वर्ग मीटर निर्मित क्षेत्र + अनुमति शुल्क स्लैब तालिका (21(3)(b)).

answer.answer:
बिल्डिंग परमिशन की फीस नियम 21 में दी गई है। यह दो हिस्सों में लगती है:
- आवेदन शुल्क (नियम 21(2)(ii)): प्रस्तावित बिल्ट-अप एरिया पर Rs 1.00 प्रति वर्ग मीटर। यह शुल्क किसी भी हाल में वापस नहीं होता।
- अनुमति शुल्क (नियम 21(3)): यह परमिशन जारी होने से पहले जमा करना होता है। सामान्य भवन के लिए नियम 21(3)(b) की स्लैब तालिका लागू होती है, जिसमें फीस बिल्ट-अप एरिया और भवन के उपयोग पर निर्भर करती है। हाई-राइज भवन के लिए नियम 21(3)(c) अलग से लागू होता है।
सही रकम निकालने के लिए नागरिक से कुल प्रस्तावित बिल्ट-अप एरिया और भवन का उपयोग पता करना होगा।
answer.ask_citizen: कृपया नागरिक से पूछें: (1) कुल प्रस्तावित बिल्ट-अप एरिया (वर्ग मीटर में) कितना है, (2) भवन किस उपयोग के लिए है (सिर्फ आवास, दुकान/व्यावसायिक, दुकान-सह-आवास आदि), और (3) क्या भवन हाई-राइज है।
